newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close flat to lower in quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close flat to lower in quiet day.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to lower Wednesday after a slow session with little inspiration found to motivate market movements.
The market rose gently in the morning and then declined slowly in the afternoon, tracking the movements of U.S. Treasuries.
"There is not much to say, there was very little activity," said a trader at an Argentine bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.01 to 122.05, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/8 to 85-3/8.
The trader added that the market is likely to remain very calm through the rest of the week, as investors close positions ahead of the Christmas and New Year period.
"I don't expect much to happen (this week)," said another trader.

This session's release of November fiscal figures showing a deficit of $843 million had no impact on the market, said traders. Nor did preliminary figures from the FIEL consultancy reporting a 13.2 percent rise in industrial production in November from the same month a year ago.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 7.50 percent from 7.75 percent.
